newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch arrest suspected shop bomb blackmailers.
newsitem.headline: Dutch arrest suspected shop bomb blackmailers.

text.p: Dutch police said on Thursday they had arrested two men suspected of blackmailing a leading department store chain and confiscated a cache of explosives.

The two men were apprehended on Tuesday night after a police surveillance unit traced a call to the Vroom & Dreesmann store chain back to a public telephone booth on Amsterdam's outskirts, spokesman Klaas Wilting said.

"The first attempt at extortion dates back to April...(The men) demanded around one million guilders ($486,000) and threatened to plant a bomb at one of the store's branches if the chain did not pay up," he said.
Wilting said house searches at the homes of the two men, which he described as known criminals in their early thirties, had uncovered a store of explosives which were subsequently deactivated.
"Thanks to close cooperation with the security management of V&D, the safety of staff and customers at the store was never at risk," Wilting said.
Vroom & Dreesmann is the flagship department store chain of Dutch retail and services group Vendex. ($ = 2.054 Dutch Guilders)
